summary: Recorded won revenue is $10,005,534 across 4,238 won deals, with an overall win rate of 63.15% and average sales per won deal of $2,360.91. Average weeks to close is 7.40. Separately, estimated open-pipeline list price is $3,360,822 across 2,089 open opportunities; 333 open opportunities are unpriced and excluded from that estimate. This is not a probability-weighted forecast. Team win rates are tightly clustered: Summer Sewald 64.34% and Cara Losch 64.43% are above the overall win rate, while Melvin Marxen 62.20% and Rocco Neubert 62.08% are below. Product conversion is led by MG Special 64.84% and GTX Plus Pro 64.30%; GTXPro leads product revenue at $3,510,578. Quarterly close revenue softened after 2017-Q2, and new opportunities fell sharply in 2017-Q4. Data caveats: 500 invalid engage dates and 333 unpriced open opportunities; GTK 500 and some agent results have small samples.
callout: New opportunities: 8,800. Open opportunities: 2,089. Estimated open-pipeline list price: $3,360,822. Unpriced open opportunities: 333. Won deals: 4,238. Closed deals: 6,711. Overall win rate: 63.15%.
data_flags: 333 open opportunities have no exact product list-price match.
500 opportunities have invalid or missing engage dates.

findings.question: How is each sales team performing compared to the rest?
findings.answer: By manager, Summer Sewald has a 64.34% win rate and Cara Losch has 64.43%, both above the overall 63.15%. Melvin Marxen is at 62.20% and Rocco Neubert at 62.08%, both below overall. Melvin Marxen has the highest won revenue at $2,251,930, followed by Summer Sewald at $1,964,750 and Rocco Neubert at $1,960,545. By region, West leads revenue at $3,568,647 with a 63.94% win rate; Central has the most opportunities at 3,512 and revenue of $3,346,293 with a 62.56% win rate; East has revenue of $3,090,594 with a 63.02% win rate.

findings.question: Are any sales agents lagging behind?
findings.answer: Overall win rate is 63.15%. Agents below overall include Lajuana Vencill 54.98%, Markita Hansen 57.27%, Donn Cantrell 57.45%, Gladys Colclough 58.19%, Niesha Huffines 60.00%, Daniell Hammack 60.96%, Garret Kinder 60.98%, Anna Snelling 61.90%, Zane Levy 61.69%, Cassey Cress 62.45%, Kary Hendrixson 62.39%, Marty Freudenburg 62.89%, and Darcel Schlecht 63.11%. Agents at or above overall include Hayden Neloms 70.39%, Maureen Marcano 69.95%, Wilburn Farren 69.62%, Cecily Lampkin 66.88%, Versie Hillebrand 66.67%, Moses Frase 66.15%, Boris Faz 66.01%, James Ascencio 65.53%, Corliss Cosme 65.50%, Rosalina Dieter 65.45%, Reed Clapper 65.40%, Jonathan Berthelot 64.77%, Rosie Papadopoulos 64.46%, Kami Bicknell 63.97%, Vicki Laflamme 63.69%, Elease Gluck 63.49%, and Violet Mclelland 63.21%. Darcel Schlecht has the highest won revenue at $1,153,214. Sample sizes vary; interpret lower-volume agents with caution.

findings.question: Are there any quarter-over-quarter trends?
findings.answer: By close quarter, 2017-Q1 had 531 won deals, $1,134,672 won revenue, and an 82.07% win rate. 2017-Q2 won revenue rose to $3,086,111 with 1,254 won deals and a 61.71% win rate; QoQ revenue change was +171.98%. 2017-Q3 revenue was $2,982,255 with 1,257 won deals and a 61.41% win rate; QoQ change was -3.37%. 2017-Q4 revenue was $2,802,496 with 1,196 won deals and a 60.25% win rate; QoQ change was -6.03%. New opportunities by engage quarter: 2016-Q4 358; 2017-Q1 1,619 (+352.23%); 2017-Q2 2,388 (+47.50%); 2017-Q3 2,770 (+16.00%); 2017-Q4 1,165 (-57.94%).

findings.question: Do any products have better win rates?
findings.answer: Product win rates: MG Special 64.84%, GTX Plus Pro 64.30%, GTX Basic 63.72%, GTXPro 63.56%, GTX Plus Basic 62.13%, MG Advanced 60.33%, and GTK 500 60.00%. GTK 500 has only 40 opportunities and 25 closed deals, so its rate is based on a small sample. GTXPro has the highest won revenue at $3,510,578, followed by GTX Plus Pro at $2,629,651 and MG Advanced at $2,216,387. MG Special has the highest win rate but lower won revenue at $43,768. MG Advanced is below the overall win rate despite high revenue.

recommendations.text: Use recorded won revenue and estimated open-pipeline list price separately; do not present probability-weighted forecasts because no opportunity probability is available.
Coach agents with lower win rates and sufficient sample sizes, such as Lajuana Vencill, Markita Hansen, Donn Cantrell, and Gladys Colclough, and review deal-level conversion drivers.
Study practices from higher win-rate agents such as Hayden Neloms, Maureen Marcano, and Wilburn Farren, while noting that some agent samples are smaller.
Investigate the 2017-Q4 drop in new opportunities and the softening close revenue and win rate after 2017-Q2 to identify pipeline generation and close-execution gaps.
Prioritize high-revenue products GTXPro and GTX Plus Pro, and assess why MG Advanced has high revenue but a below-overall win rate.
Evaluate MG Special for conversion strength versus low revenue, including pricing, upsell, or product-mix opportunities.
Target high-performing sectors such as retail, technolgy, software, and marketing, and review finance and medical conversion performance.
Protect and expand top accounts Kan-code, Konex, Condax, Cheers, and Hottechi, especially in software, technolgy, medical, and entertainment.
Improve data quality by addressing 500 invalid engage dates and 333 unpriced open opportunities so reporting and pipeline estimates are more complete.
Treat GTK 500 and lower-volume agent results as small samples and avoid overgeneralizing from them.
